why: Order was auto-cancelled by the 60-min hold-stock timer at 14:13:00, 41s BEFORE the payment was captured at 14:13:41. The 504s at 14:13:43 are real but irrelevant: even an instant webhook would have hit an already-cancelled order, which is exactly what the 14:15 retry shows (200, plugin skips because cancelled). Merchant note pushes endpoint_timeout; ordering rules it out.

Every delivery from 10:02 onward got a ~40ms 403 HTML page and the plugin never logged a single webhook.received, so requests were stopped before WordPress/plugin code (security layer: Wordfence rate-limit/UA blocking). The Razorpay-mentioning PHP fatal is at 12:47, nearly 3h after the first failed delivery, in the child theme's thank-you hook, and deliveries after it are still 403 not 500. Cron logs 'no pending webhook requests' because nothing was ever received, so not cron. Merchant note is a red herring.

Razorpay attempted delivery 2s after capture (14:10:07); the merchant endpoint hit 30s 504s at 14:10 and 14:15 while a 1-PHP-worker shared host was under a flash sale. The 14:50 arrival is Razorpay's backoff retry succeeding, not platform delay. Merchant's 'nothing changed, Razorpay is late' note is misleading.

Razorpay delivered both events with fast 200s, but there is no plugin telemetry, wp_cron status is unreported, and the site just moved hosts and added a page cache. 200-but-not-updated fits a cache serving the webhook URL (theme_plugin_conflict), a queued webhook never processed (wp_cron_not_running), or the webhook URL still pointing at the old host/another install. Nothing in the evidence separates these; need plugin debug log, cron status and confirmation of which server answered the webhook URL.
